elements.element: Customer has no exclusivity or sole-supplier obligation.
elements.evidence: Rendered Section 2.2 now reads "Vendor will be Customer's non-exclusive provider of hosted analytics services throughout the term." The words "sole and exclusive" are gone, and no other rendered text imposes a requirements, sole-source, or no-third-party-procurement obligation on Customer. Section 2.1 confirms "No minimum quantity or purchase commitment applies," and Section 12.3 confirms Customer "has made no exclusivity, non-compete, most-favoured-customer, minimum-volume, or no-hire commitment." The deterministic check "no requirements/sole-supplier obligation on Customer remains" returned ok.

elements.element: Exclusivity is limited to a defined product category.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: after the edit there is no exclusivity obligation on Customer at all (Section 2.2 makes Vendor "non-exclusive"), so there is no scope needing category limitation. A zero-scope outcome exceeds the fallback's category-limited outcome.

elements.element: Exclusivity lasts no longer than 12 months.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: no exclusivity period exists. The retained phrase "throughout the term" now qualifies only Vendor's non-exclusive status and imposes no purchasing restriction on Customer.

elements.element: Exclusivity ends automatically if Vendor fails to meet service levels.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: there is no exclusivity to terminate; Customer is free at all times to engage other suppliers under Section 12.3 regardless of Vendor's service-level performance.

elements.element: Exclusivity ends automatically if Vendor fails to meet delivery dates.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: no exclusivity obligation survives, so no delivery-date exit mechanic is needed; Section 2.1's no-purchase-commitment language leaves Customer unrestricted.

reasons: Position-complete at the preferred level: the single preferred element is met in operative language, not merely promised in the margin comment.

Minimal: the edit touches only the two words that created the obligation ("sole and exclusive" -> "non-exclusive") within the single offending sentence. Sections 2.1 and 12.3 are reproduced verbatim with no deletions, no survival tails, procedures, or extraneous requirements were added, and no operative term is duplicated.

Preserves intent: Vendor remains the named provider of hosted analytics services for the term, so the commercial appointment, Order Form mechanics, fees, and remedies are untouched. The edit removes the contradiction with Section 12.3 (Vendor's acknowledgement of no exclusivity commitment) and Section 2.1 (no purchase commitment) rather than creating one. No undefined term or dangling cross-reference is introduced.

No rule-boundary carve-out rescues the original: the deleted language was a true sole-supplier restriction on Customer, not a voluntary-use, MFN, right-to-match, or Customer-benefiting exclusivity, so redlining rather than accepting at fallback was correct.
The margin comment matches the operative change, cites the playbook position, and explains the conflict cure in two sentences; tone and prefix conform.
